solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something done about dolly became harder to get?

indicators.note: something placed about another wraps round it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a deed is a thing done
to dolly is to beat with a tool; pene is a Chambers spelling of peen, to hammer

explanation.surface: Someone tinkering with a doll finds the task getting trickier.
explanation.walkthrough: DEE + PENE + D. The question mark covers the definition: a puzzle or mystery that deepened became harder to get to the bottom of.
explanation.definitionFit: When a mystery deepens it grows more profound and so more difficult to understand.

clue.text: With one steamer departing doubt remains

indicators.note: things departing leave, so those letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to doubt is to distrust
Roman numeral one
str. is the dictionary abbreviation for steamer

explanation.surface: As a boat sails away, some lingering uncertainty is left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and STR out of DISTRUST and DUST is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust is what is left of a body after death, as in ashes to ashes, so it means mortal remains.

clue.text: Cassio's to go round forming new list

indicators.note: forming means shaping into something, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a ship that lists heels over

explanation.surface: Cassio is to do the rounds, drawing up a fresh roster.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassio, a character in Othello, marks the word as Shakespearean: Shakespeare used enwheel once, in that play.
explanation.definitionFit: To enwheel is to encircle or encompass, which is going round something.

clue.text: Pressure on witticism lifting union agreement?

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
re means on or about

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word turns it upside down so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: Pressure and wordplay are used to lift a trade union deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but here it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenup is a contract made before a marriage, the union in question, settling property in case of divorce.

clue.text: Pay up for heating vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid into the pot at poker

explanation.surface: Settle the bill for a kettle or boiler.
explanation.definitionFit: An etna is a small vessel for heating liquids over a spirit flame, named after the volcano.

clue.text: Grey one's turning out sweets

indicators.note: turning something out rearranges it, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: letters as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A grey-haired confectioner is making sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Eryngoes are candied roots of sea holly, once eaten as sweetmeats.

clue.text: Rector's away making rubbishy composing, as before

indicators.note: when someone is away they are absent, so that letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: to dirt is to make dirty
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: With the vicar absent, the hymn writing turns into rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks an archaic word: dite is an old verb meaning to compose, as in indite.
explanation.definitionFit: Diting is the old present participle of dite, to write or compose a text.

clue.text: Head off to visit relative

indicators.note: taking the head off a word removes its first letter

parts.note: to haunt a place is to visit it often

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave and call on a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family relation.

clue.text: Otherwise again good to go about neat lack of vital sine qua non?

definitions.text: lack of vital sine qua non?

indicators.note: letters placed about something wrap round it
otherwise means in another way, so the word is set out in another order
a letter that has to go is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: A rambling sentence about something essential that keeps going missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle that survives in neatsfoot oil. The vital sine qua non is oxygen, the thing life cannot do without.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoxia is an absence of oxygen in the body, oxygen being the indispensable condition for life.

clue.text: Out again ringing royal one up in millions of cases?

parts.note: someone out cold is under, unconscious

indicators.note: ringing something means circling it, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: then can mean again, in the sense of on the other hand

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the royal we makes one monarch speak as us

explanation.surface: Once more a royal is circled by those who might count the cases.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal we lets a single monarch be US. The definition plays on the sun shining on millions of cases: wherever it shines, that is anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the sun means anywhere on earth, so it covers every one of countless instances.

clue.text: Charge is very informally beyond doubt

parts.note: tres, from French, is a jokey English word for very
certain

explanation.surface: A statement that the accusation definitely stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like an accusation or a price, but it is a heraldic term for a figure on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a tressure is a narrow inner border on a shield, one of the charges borne on it.

clue.text: Change course with career causing harm?

parts.note: to wear a ship is to turn it onto the other tack by bringing the wind behind
and means together with
to career is to rush along, to tear

explanation.surface: Switching jobs mid-career has done some damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change course' and 'career' look like talk of jobs; they are sailing and speeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear and tear is the damage things suffer from ordinary use over time.

clue.text: Who smiles? Gross boozer in front of the Queen

parts.note: gr. is the abbreviation for gross
a boozer is British slang for a pub
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A puzzled look around a pub where a vulgar drinker faces the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross boozer' reads as a coarse drunk; the two words split, an abbreviation and a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinner is a person who grins, and grinning is smiling broadly.

clue.text: Rapid reaction force radically (yes) endowed with bit of temerity

indicators.note: radically means in a thoroughgoing, root-and-branch way, so these letters are thoroughly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: only a small bit of that word, its opening letter, is used

parts.note: the first letter of temerity

explanation.surface: A police strike squad is boldly given a radical makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is Cockney rhyming slang for the Flying Squad, the London police unit for fast response to armed crime, usually shortened to the Sweeney.
explanation.definitionFit: Through rhyming slang the name stands for the Flying Squad, a police unit sent out quickly to serious crime.

clue.text: First of the Chinese that expresses joy finding Chennai's station

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of the
the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
an exclamation of delight

explanation.surface: A Chinese traveller gives a happy cry on reaching a station in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Chennai, in India, signals an Indian word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thana is a police station in India, so the station in an Indian city such as Chennai.

clue.text: Run in spirits losing international earners for Irish?

indicators.note: a word losing something has those letters taken away
one letter is placed in the other word, inside it

parts.note: nixies are water sprites of Germanic folklore
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Smuggling drink across the border earns some Irish people a living.
explanation.walkthrough: Put R into NIXIES to get NIXIERS, then drop one I.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish slang a nixer is a spare-time job done for cash, an off-the-books earner.

clue.text: Disconcerting earful for staff of command

indicators.note: disconcerting means throwing into disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Officers get an unsettling telling-off from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff of command' reads like senior officers; it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferula is a rod or staff, including a ruler's sceptre carried as a symbol of authority.

clue.text: Nothing in reduced excuse will support weary staff

indicators.note: one letter is put in the other word, inside it
something reduced is cut down, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: to flag is to tire
a plea is an excuse offered
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A feeble excuse won't help tired workers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece supporting another sits below it, so FLAG comes first. 'staff' looks like employees but is a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagpole is a tall staff from which a flag is flown.

clue.text: Overbearing being egregious about matter that's been raised

indicators.note: a word placed about another goes round it

parts.note: both mean flagrant, utter

indicators.note: in a down clue, something raised is turned upward, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: go can mean an affair or state of things, as in a rum go

explanation.surface: Someone is domineering and outrageous about a subject someone else brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: A rum go is old British slang for a strange business, which is how go can mean matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrogant person is haughty and domineering, which is what overbearing describes.

clue.text: Plant is Irish in the first place

parts.note: Ir. is the abbreviation for Irish; the run of the answer inside this word is a coincidence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that some plant was originally from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the first place' puts the Irish piece at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a flowering plant with sword-shaped leaves, including the flag iris.

clue.text: As locals have it net depression results in this game

parts.note: in dialect a leap is a basket, especially a wicker fish trap
a frog is the hollow pressed into the face of a brick

explanation.surface: Locals say a net-cord slump leads to this sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As locals have it' flags a dialect word. The brick sense of frog is a builder's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game in which players vault over others who bend down.

clue.text: Separate and plunge once

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to split off a company from a merged group
second meaning: an obsolete verb, to plunge or immerse

explanation.surface: Instructions for parting things and then dunking them a single time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' is not one time but a signal of an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerge means to undo a merger, and in older use, from Latin mergere, it meant to sink or immerse.

clue.text: Mahmood's last in bat, with one wicket remaining, giving a nod of readiness

indicators.note: leaving just one of a repeated letter means the duplicate is struck out
only a single copy is left remaining, so the other copy is dropped
that letter goes in the longer word, inside it

parts.note: cricket bats are made of willow

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of Mahmood
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: the bowler Mahmood comes in to bat with one wicket left and nods.
explanation.walkthrough: Put D inside WILLOW, then keep only one of its two Ws. Saqib Mahmood is an England cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Will do is a casual reply agreeing to carry out a request, a spoken nod of readiness.

clue.text: Scope in Latin according to assiduous advocate

indicators.note: one word sits in the other, inside it

parts.note: per is Latin for according to, as in per the rules
range or extent

explanation.surface: A dedicated champion of the classics argues for broader study of Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher urges a cause with zeal, so a tireless advocate of it.

clue.text: Positive positions for those of the working class

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for positive
posts or jobs

explanation.surface: Good jobs going to manual workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Proles, short for proletarians, is an informal word for members of the working class.

clue.text: Adult in charge, an early Asian prince

indicators.note: one letter goes in the other word, inside it

parts.note: chg. is the abbreviation for charge
A is the film certificate for adult
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up took charge of a young Asian prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagan is an old form of khan, the title of a Mongol or Tartar ruler.

clue.text: No longer stick with current rajah's seat

parts.note: gad is an obsolete word for a stick or goad
I is the physics symbol for current

explanation.surface: An Indian ruler's throne can no longer be held on to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete word rather than a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadi is the cushioned throne of an Indian ruler.

clue.text: Fine to avoid woman in the legal profession on school project

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it, so the second-named piece comes first

parts.note: sch. is the abbreviation for school

indicators.note: a letter told to avoid the word stays out of it, so it is removed

parts.note: feme is the law French word for woman used in English law
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A female lawyer dodges a penalty while doing a school assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B places A after B. 'woman in the legal profession' sounds like a female lawyer; it means the word for woman in legal language.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a planned undertaking, the same as a project.

clue.text: Scaffolder's support added to report

parts.note: put in, as an ingredient is added
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A note about scaffolding equipment appended to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A putlog is one of the short horizontal timbers of a scaffold whose end rests in a hole in the wall.

clue.text: Date Milton's previously mentioned wiped out

parts.note: a period of time
sed is Milton's spelling of said, which means previously mentioned

explanation.surface: A date from Milton cited earlier has been struck out.
explanation.definitionFit: Erased means rubbed out, removed completely so nothing remains.

clue.text: Centre for arrivals opening in Lerwick?

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, with the ends dropped

parts.note: the middle four of eight letters

explanation.surface: A new arrivals hall is opening at the Shetland port.
explanation.walkthrough: Lerwick, the capital of Shetland, flags a Shetland or Orkney dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orkney and Shetland a riva is a cleft or fissure in rock, a natural opening.

clue.text: Driver accepting gold challenge in the Highlands

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: dr. is the abbreviation for driver
chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A driver takes on a gold-medal challenge in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the Highlands' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Daur is the Scots form of dare, to challenge someone to do something.

clue.text: Buzz about dress and, well, a good impression

parts.note: to give someone a buzz or a bell is to phone them
a. is an abbreviation for about
to fig out is to dress up, as in full fig
ur is a hesitant noise like well
taken as written

explanation.surface: Phoning about an outfit, well, to look good.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone a bell is British slang for a phone call. Bella figura is Italian for cutting a fine figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Bella figura means a fine appearance or favourable impression, the effect of looking and behaving well.

clue.text: Main ensign becomes dull

parts.note: lead as an adjective means main, as in the lead story
ens. is the abbreviation for ensign

explanation.surface: The principal naval flag fades.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaden is to turn the colour or heaviness of lead, so to grow dull.

clue.text: Regret spinning old coinage

indicators.note: spinning something round turns it to face the other way, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Lamenting the old money that has been spun out of circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old coinage' suggests a past currency; old is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency of most EU countries, a system of money.

clue.text: Strong passion in pilgrim?

parts.note: str. is an abbreviation for strong
a passion can be a fit of rage

explanation.surface: A pilgrim burns with intense religious feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passion' in a pilgrim suggests religious fervour; it is rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is a traveller in a foreign land, so a newcomer and stranger there.
